title: Review of c04's dividing crawlers: replicated on seeds 5 and 6 (generation 5 and 4, up to 35 BL); chi=0 caps motion at 3.3 BL
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged (claim parameters as defaults) on fresh seeds 5 and 6 with the claim's labkit settings (240 frames, threshold 0.25), and chi=0 (WORLD_P, as the author's ablation) on seed 5. Seed 5: 8 persistent splits, max generation 5, 0 merges, 13 cells at t=600, top tracks 34.7/28.4/17.0 body lengths. Seed 6: 9 persistent splits, generation 4, 1 merge, top tracks 16.0/14.2/13.7 BL. The sheet shows the founder turning into a crescent crawler by t=25 and crescent crawlers that grow, pinch and separate through t~400, then rounding up into a static lattice as the nutrient (green) runs out. chi=0 on seed 5: 20 persistent splits, generation 5, but max 3.3 BL (top five 3.3-1.6).

observations.I: rerun/seed5/sheet.png: discrete crescent cells, 13 at t=600
observations.M: rerun/seed5/metrics.json motion_top: 34.7, 28.4, 17.0 BL; sheet t=25-300 crescents crawling with the body plan kept
observations.D: rerun/seed5/lineage.png: 8 persistent splits to generation 5, 0 merges; seed 6: 9 splits, generation 4

verdicts.limitation: Planted, kicked founder (no S). Motility belongs to the fed phase: after t~400 the cells round up and freeze, so late-generation divisions are of near-static cells. Body content is per-body bookkeeping and division uses a finite-range (nonlocal) area penalty. I did not re-run the lamOK=0 division ablation.
